notes.title: Demo is now available!

notes.title: Mr. Nomad Demo Playtest Sign-Ups Are Now Open!
notes.notes:
[p]Greetings Nomads![/p][p][/p][p]We’re excited to announce that sign-ups are now open for the Mr. Nomad Demo playtest! This is your chance to experience the game with other testers before anyone else and help shape its future. We’re looking for enthusiastic players who are eager to provide feedback and contribute to making Mr. Nomad the best it can be.[/p][p][/p][p]By joining the demo playtest, you’ll gain early access to gameplay (singleplayer and multiplayer) and a chance to explore new world as Mr. Nomad. Your feedback will be incredibly valuable to us, whether it’s about balancing, features, bugs, or overall enjoyment. By giving us your feedback and suggestions you'll also be part of the development process![/p][p][/p][p]No experience is necessary! Players of all backgrounds and skill levels are welcome! All you need is a willingness to play, share your honest thoughts, and engage with our development team. Selected participants will receive instructions on how to access the demo playtest and how to share their feedback.[/p][p][/p][p]If you’re interested in being part of our community and making a real impact on the development of Mr. Nomad, [b]Sign Up Now[/b]! notes.title: DEV_log #4 Multiplayer
notes.notes:
[b]Hey, fellow Nomads! [/b]

We’ve got some another updates on the development of Mr. Nomad! Our co-op mode is coming together fast, and we’re getting it ready for the upcoming demo. Right now, it’s in a very advanced state, and we’re putting it through rigorous testing to ensure a smooth and immersive experience.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44689949/a83e191be7010fc75a4f781466a5291910e9ae54.gif[/img]

From synchronizing player movements to refining network stability, we’re making sure that playing together feels as seamless and engaging as possible. Our goal is to bring you a multiplayer experience that truly enhances the unique fighting and building mechanics of Mr. Nomad.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44689949/71d8c73743a2788edd00ae8d41a2a4dbdb39ad4d.gif[/img]

Stay tuned for more updates, and as always, thank you for being part of this journey!

notes.title: DEV_log #3
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44689949/f19c11cfe68b2a5a0da12456fa18c8d6369f5a47.png[/img]
[h2]Hello, fellow Nomads![/h2]

We're currently developing a diverse lineup of zombie types that players must face. Each one has its own unique characteristics and poses different challenges during gameplay. Below, we’ll go over the different kinds of zombies you can encounter, but for now, let’s just say you’ll need to be prepared for anything!

[h3]The Roamer[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44689949/0e9c233235fda0515b966bc179c66b14db18a56b.png[/img]
This is our most common enemy that Nomads will encounter while  playing the game, he doesn't seem that dangerous as the others  but you should still be careful because after all he's still a zombie,  right? 

[h3]The Butcher[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44689949/ba8a70f5e0e1d16a627c78e923b6c046a3ab4002.png[/img]
Oi mate, it's the Butcher, don't lose your head. He is known for  throwing a chopper at the player and is stronger than the last  zombie. Don't worry though he will spawn more rarely. 

[h3]The Exploder[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44689949/e6066ea68a1ab1a1c4f44ece9798ed5de2f9c646.png[/img]
Our bomb looking friend, well... i guess we all know what he will do,  right?
In case you don't he explodes his barrel! 

[h3]The Sprinter[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44689949/416acaebfbdbbff7734ce6d59683823f05af47ec.png[/img]
Former Olympian perhaps, a Sprinter himself, he's really fast which  makes him really hard to outrun. 

[h3]The General[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44689949/58fa5f05702cbd720db88462ea6fb94fed58a888.png[/img]
Beware! A giant zombie joined the fight! We think of him as a boss,  he's strong, has a lot of hp and more importantly wields a giant  tank gun. 

That's it! We hope you enjoyed the enemies you'll be facing in the  game. Stay tuned for more updates, and don't forget to tell us what  you'd like to see in the next devlog. Stay alive! 

[h3]They're coming for you![/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44689949/d719512fcc40bcea93200afea4a7236ece23cea5.gif[/img]

notes.title: DEV_log #2
notes.notes:
[b]Hey, fellow Nomads! [/b]

Today, we’re excited to [b]share some insights into the procedural generation aspect of Mr. Nomad[/b]. It’s one of our core tools, allowing us to shape the numerous challenges ahead of you while leaving us in control of the specifics of what you’ll encounter in the post-apocalyptic world.

[b]Beware![/b] Some technical jargon is about to appear on your screen, but it’s all basically about how we make things random.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44689949/25068d0cb66ca5ee427741ed53b3cf0faad8fdb8.png[/img]
[i]How it's made?[/i]

The procedural aspect of [b]Mr. Nomad[/b] is powered by [b]Vista[/b], a useful tool that we’ve tailored to our needs. We’ve used it to generate the terrain of the game’s main locations, where the initial Points of Interest (POIs) are located. 

While doing this, we’re able to pre-determine certain rules for the game world. We set elevation maps, decide where certain rock formations should appear, preset biomes, set spawn locations for different assets (i.e. lootable cars near a national road) or what the initial resources accessible to players should be so that they can start the game properly (like Agave plants spawning to provide the player with a source of fiber).

Our use of this Procedural Content Generation forms the foundation of what Mr. Nomad offers and how it will change and adapt over time. We’re a passionate team, but we’re not an AAA developer, so managing our available resources is crucial. [b]This system allows us to develop and seamlessly integrate major additions while staying fully in control of everything.[/b] Presenting you with a sprawling world of possibilities and balancing it at the same time is a lot simpler with proper tools. 



We’ve also implemented [b]Forward Plus Rendering[/b] to enhance the visual experience. What does it do?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44689949/ca048c887ae83ccd4230d8ddfdadee1927981d72.png[/img]
[i]Before...[/i]


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44689949/99b6d71f446d43f4826ae67ca336a6c6ef6e112f.png[/img]
[i]...and after![/i]

[b]Simple version[/b]: Forward Plus lowers memory overhead because it doesn’t require storing intermediate data in G-buffers like deferred lighting does. Ok, this doesn’t sound all that simple to me, let’s try again.

[b]Also a simple version, but for a different audience:[/b] this means there’s very little in terms of limit on the light sources in the game, nicely illuminating both you and the zombies coming to get you without compromising performance.

[b]The simplest version[/b]: better light, same FPS What’s not to love?[i]*[/i]



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44689949/ddfa3c861401fc729d45c9a86c3209f82eeb55f7.png[/img]
[i]You dirty, dirty dirt, you![/i]


Another field where we implemented procedural generation tools is textures. We’re using stochastic texturing, meaning that[b] the exact color of each pixel is randomized, to a degree[/b], leading to something that looks unique and irregular, instead of resembling a repeated pattern (you know, like when you look at something distant in a video game and the textures looks as if someone copypasted them in regular intervals). Our tools allow us to also do triplanar texturing that [b]prevents visible seams between textures[/b] on 3d objects. 

Some of the textures represent for example slopes or erosion, to increase the variation further. Terrain tiles that we create this way can later be used to create large, rich, and diverse environments to explore with your trusty RV, without making different locations too similar.



That’s it! We hope this gives you a glimpse into the process behind [b]Mr. Nomad[/b]. Stay tuned for more updates as we continue to prepare our RV to ram straight through the horde. 

Make sure to let us know what topics you’d like to see us cover next and in the meantime, [b]stay alive![/b]



[i]*Let us know which version you liked best, nomads, we’ll make sure to write ALL our devlogs this way!
[/i]
